claims.claim: The proposal requests 420,000 ADA plus a 105,000 ADA contingency reserve to fund a part-time Oura maintainer over 12 months at an annual rate of $105,000 USD.
The total treasury withdrawal is 540,750 ADA, consisting of 525,000 ADA for Oura maintenance and enhancement and a 15,750 ADA Intersect budget administration fee.
Oura connects to Cardano nodes, monitors blockchain events, and routes matching patterns to pluggable outputs for processing.
Oura supports multiple data sources including N2C, N2N, S3, Mithril, and UTxO RPC, and supports sinks including Kafka, Elasticsearch, AWS Lambda/S3/SQS, RabbitMQ, Redis, SQL databases, and webhooks.
Oura has 654 commits, 288 stars, 79 forks, and 58 contributors, and is the most starred project in the TxPipe portfolio.
Oura has previously been funded twice through Project Catalyst, in Fund 9 and Fund 13, for feature development.
The proposal achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase.
The requested amount did not, at submission, breach the applicable 350M ADA Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713.
TxPipe has received funding through 30 Project Catalyst proposals across Funds 9 through 14, with 26 successfully delivered and 4 currently under development and on schedule.
Independent oversight for treasury administration will be provided by Intersect and technically capable third parties, with reporting obligations and milestone-based disbursement controls.

summary: The document requests 540,750 ADA for 12 months of Oura maintenance through Intersect-managed smart contracts, provides high-level scope, budget line items, governance-process references, smart-contract addresses, and oversight structure, but the deterministic assessment records missing treasury, feasibility, risk, alternatives, and failure-mode analysis.
